subtype: Child who seeks comfort and returns to play [Actor]
passage: At the park in Accra, five-year-old Kofi tripped on the slide steps and scraped his knee. He ran straight to his mum on the bench, crying loudly. She held him, blew on the scrape and said, "Ouch. That hurt, didn't it?" He sniffed, nodded, then pointed at his friend Hiroshi on the swings. "Can I go back?" "Go on." Walking home later, Kofi said, "Mum, I pulled Hiroshi's kite string and it broke. I didn't mean to." "Thank you for telling me. Shall we help fix it tomorrow?" Kofi nodded, relieved, and swung her hand.

qa.q: How did Kofi hurt his knee?
qa.a: He tripped on the slide steps and scraped his knee.

qa.q: Why did Kofi tell his mum about the kite without being asked?
qa.a: He trusts she will help rather than blame him, so he isn't afraid to tell.

qa.q: What did Kofi's mum do after hearing about the kite, and why does it matter?
qa.a: She thanked him for telling and offered to help fix it, which keeps him willing to share problems.

qa.q: How might Hiroshi feel if Kofi helps fix the kite tomorrow?
qa.a: Hiroshi may feel cared for and quickly forgive the broken string.

grounding: A hurt child runs to his mother, is calmed and goes back to play, and later tells her about a problem without fear of blame.

passage: At the community centre's Saturday art class, five-year-old Ritu bumped her head on the table corner and burst into tears. She ran straight to her mother, Lavanya, on the bench, and cried into her shoulder. Lavanya held her and pressed a cool hand to the bump. "That surprised you. I've got you." Ritu cried a little, then sat up. "Can I finish my peacock?" Before going back she whispered, "Amma, Tanay took my blue crayon." Lavanya said, "Thank you for telling me. Let's ask the teacher to help you both share." Ritu nodded and went back to her peacock.

qa.q: What did Ritu want to finish?
qa.a: Her peacock.

qa.q: What does Ritu sitting up and asking to finish her peacock show?
qa.a: She feels calm and safe again after being comforted, and ready to play.

qa.q: What did Lavanya do when Ritu mentioned the crayon?
qa.a: She thanked her for telling and offered to ask the teacher to help them share.

qa.q: How might the art teacher feel when Lavanya asks for help with the crayon?
qa.a: The teacher may be glad to know early and help the children share calmly.

grounding: A hurt five-year-old runs to her mother, is calmed and returns to her painting, and tells her about a small problem without fear.

subtype: Child who seeks comfort and returns to play [Actor]
passage: The train to Madurai was two hours late, and the platform was packed. Kavitha was hopping between the yellow lines when a boy running past knocked her down. She scraped her knee on the concrete and ran straight to Appa, howling. Siddharth pulled her onto his lap, blew on the scrape and held her until the sobs slowed. 'A boy pushed me,' she said. 'He didn't say sorry.' 'Thank you for telling me,' said Appa. 'That wasn't your fault.' Kavitha sniffed, looked at her knee, then slid off his lap and went back to hopping, further from the edge.

qa.q: How late was the train?
qa.a: Two hours.

qa.q: Why did Kavitha run straight to Appa?
qa.a: She was hurt and scared, and trusted that Appa would comfort her.

qa.q: What did Siddharth say that helps Kavitha keep telling him things?
qa.a: 'Thank you for telling me. That wasn't your fault,' showing she won't be blamed for sharing a problem.

qa.q: How might the boy who knocked Kavitha down have felt?
qa.a: He may not have noticed in the crowd, or felt a little guilty, but he ran on without saying sorry.

grounding: Shows a young child who runs to a parent when hurt, is calmed, tells him about a problem without fear of blame, and returns to play.

passage: Zubin was racing his cars under the dining table in their Dadar flat when he sat up too fast. Bang. He ran to Lavanya in the kitchen, wailing, holding his head. She knelt and held him, rubbing the spot. 'Ouch. Big bump.' He cried into her shoulder until his breathing slowed, then ran back to his cars. That evening he came in from the building compound looking serious. 'Mummy, my ball broke Mrs. Irani's flowerpot. I didn't mean to.' 'Thank you for telling me,' Lavanya said. 'Let's go and say sorry together.'

qa.q: How did Zubin seem to feel when he told Lavanya about the flowerpot?
qa.a: He looked serious and a little worried, but not afraid to tell her.

qa.q: How might Mrs. Irani feel when Zubin comes to say sorry?
qa.a: She would probably be touched by the honest apology, even if sorry about the flowerpot.

passage:
'Mumma! Mumma! It bit me!'
Varun came running from the sandpit, holding out his hand, tears pouring.
Deepika scooped him up. 'Let me see. Oh, a red ant. That stings.'
'It hurts!'
'I know. Let's wash it.' She poured water from her bottle over his hand and held him close. 'Better?'
He hiccuped. 'A bit.'
'Want to stay with me or go back?'
He looked at the sandpit. 'Back. But Mumma, a big boy took my spade.'
'Thanks for telling me. Shall I come and ask for it?'
'Yes.'
They walked over, and soon Varun was digging again.

qa.q: What bit Varun?
qa.a: A red ant.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling when he ran to Deepika?
qa.a: He was hurt and upset, crying from the sting.

qa.q: How did Deepika help Varun get back to play?
qa.a: She comforted him and washed the sting, asked if he wanted to go back, and helped with the spade problem he told her about.

qa.q: What might the big boy with the spade feel when Deepika asks for it?
qa.a: He might feel a little embarrassed or caught out, and hand it back.

grounding: Shows a young child who runs to a parent when hurt, is soothed, returns to play, and tells her about a problem expecting help rather than blame.

passage:
From Pankaj's Amma's notebook, Sunday.
At the park, Pankaj fell off the low wall and scraped his knee. He ran to me shouting "Amma!", crying hard. I held him, blew on the scrape and said, "That hurt, na." Soon his crying slowed. He looked at the knee, then ran back to the swings.
At bedtime he said, "Amma, Rukmini in my class pulls my bag every day. I don't like it."
I thanked him for telling me. Tomorrow I'll speak to his teacher.

qa.q: What happened to Pankaj at the park?
qa.a: He fell off the low wall and scraped his knee.

qa.q: How did Pankaj feel when he fell, and what helped?
qa.a: He was hurt and upset, crying hard, and being held and hearing "That hurt, na" helped him calm down.

qa.q: What did Amma do well at bedtime?
qa.a: She thanked Pankaj for telling her about Rukmini and planned to speak to his teacher, so he learns telling is safe.

qa.q: What would change if Amma had scolded Pankaj for crying at the park?
qa.a: He might learn that showing hurt brings blame, and he might keep problems like the bag-pulling to himself instead of telling her.

grounding: Shows a child who runs to his mother when hurt, is calmed and returns to play, and tells her about a problem without fear of blame.
